column2: 中古英语 throwen ← 古英语 þrāwan（扭、转）← 原始日耳曼语 *þrēaną（拧、转）← 原始印欧语 *terh₁-（搓、拧）；本义是拧，后转为掷
column3: to send something through the air with a movement of the arm
column5: He threw the ball across the yard.|She threw her coat onto the bed.
column6: sending something flying by a sweep of the arm – 手臂一挥，把东西送上天飞出去
column7: 扔：随手抛出|投掷：使力掷向目标，多见于比赛|抛：轻轻送出，多带弧线

column2: 中古英语 þristen ← 古诺尔斯语 þrysta（挤、压）← 原始日耳曼语 *þrustijaną，或出自原始印欧语 *trewd-（挤、压）
column3: to push something suddenly and hard
column5: He thrust the door open with his shoulder.|The engine gives enormous thrust.
column6: one sudden hard push in a single direction – 朝一个方向猛地一推
column7: 猛推：一下用力推出|推力：这一推所产生的力|塞进：把东西硬推入窄处

column2: 中古英语 thombe ← 古英语 þūma ← 原始日耳曼语 *þūmô ← 原始印欧语 *tum-（长大、变粗），本义是「粗的那根」
column3: the short thick finger set apart from the other four
column5: He pressed the clay flat with his thumb.|She hurt her thumb closing the door.
column6: the short thick digit that works against the other four – 又短又粗、能与其余四指相对的那根

column2: 中古英语 thunder ← 古英语 þunor ← 原始日耳曼语 *þunraz ← 原始印欧语 *(s)tenh₂-（轰响）；与 stun、astonish 同支
column3: the loud noise that follows lightning
column5: Thunder rolled across the valley.|We heard thunder long before the rain.
column6: the deep roar that comes after the flash – 闪光过后传来的那阵低沉巨响
column7: 雷：这种天象|雷声：它发出的那个声响|轰响：把这种声音用到别的巨响上

column2: 古英语 Þunresdæġ（雷神之日），仿拉丁语 dies Iovis（朱庇特之日）而造；Þunor 即北欧雷神 Thor
column3: the fourth day of the working week, after Wednesday
column5: The meeting is on Thursday.|She flies out next Thursday morning.
column6: the day named after the god of thunder – 以雷神命名的那一天

column2: 中古英语 tek（轻触、轻敲）← 古英语 *ticcian（轻碰）← 原始西日耳曼语 *tikkōn（轻触）；「蜱」是另一支，← 古英语 ticia
column3: a short light sound made by a clock, or a small mark showing something is correct
column5: The clock ticked in the empty hall.|Put a tick beside each finished item.
column6: one short light contact, heard or drawn – 短而轻的一下，听见的或画下的
column7: 嘀嗒：钟表走动发出的那一声|勾号：纸上打的那一小笔，表示对|蜱虫：另一支同形异源的词，指那种吸血小虫

column2: 借自中古法语 etiquet／estiquette（票据、标签）← 古法语 estechier（贴、插）← 法兰克语 *stikkjan（刺、插）；与 etiquette 同源
column3: a printed piece of paper showing you have paid or may enter
column5: He bought two tickets for the concert.|She got a parking ticket on Friday.
column6: a slip that proves a right to enter or ride – 一张纸片，凭它证明有权进场或乘坐
column7: 票：付过钱的凭证|入场券：专指凭它进场的那种|罚单：交警贴的那张纸，形制相同而用途相反

column2: 中古英语 tyde ← 古英语 tīd（时候、时节）← 原始日耳曼语 *tīdiz；与 time 同支，本指定时而来之事，后专指潮水
column3: the regular rise and fall of the sea
column5: The tide comes in twice a day.|The tide of opinion turned against him.
column6: the sea's regular rise and fall, coming on its own clock – 海水按自己的钟涨落
column7: 潮：这种涨落现象|潮水：涨落中那股水本身|趋势：把「按时涨落、势不可挡」用到人心与局面上

column2: 中古英语 tidy（合时的、应季的），即 tide（时候）＋ 形容词后缀 -y；词义由「合时」转为「整齐」
column3: arranged neatly, with everything in place
column5: Her desk is always tidy.|Please keep the kitchen tidy.
column6: everything put where it belongs – 每样东西都在该在的位置上
column7: 整齐的：摆放有序，看着不乱|收拾干净的：经人整理过之后的那种状态

column2: 中古英语 teye（绳、链）← 古英语 tēag ← 原始日耳曼语 *taugō ← 原始印欧语 *dewk-（牵、拉）
column3: to fasten something with string or rope, or a strip of cloth worn at the neck
column5: Tie the parcel with strong string.|The match ended in a tie.
column6: drawing two ends together and fixing them – 把两头拉到一处并固定住
column7: 系紧：把两端拉紧扣住|领带：颈前那条布，本身就靠打结固定|平局：两方比分被「拉平」，如同两头系到一处

column2: 中古英语 tygre，部分承古英语 tigras，部分 ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 tigre ← 拉丁语 tigris ← 希腊语 tigris ← 伊朗语支
column3: a large wild cat with orange fur and black stripes
column5: A tiger crossed the clearing at dusk.|Tigers hunt alone, not in packs.
column6: a large striped cat that hunts alone – 身有条纹、独来独往的大型猫科猛兽
column7: 虎：书面或复合词里的说法|老虎：日常口语的叫法

column2: 中古英语 tight，为 thight 的变体 ← 古英语 *þīht ← 原始日耳曼语 *þinhtaz ← 原始印欧语 *tenkt-（密、紧）← *ten-（拉伸）
column3: fixed or pulled so firmly that there is no slack
column5: The knot was too tight to undo.|Money has been tight since the move.
column6: drawn so taut that nothing can slip – 拉到绷住，一点也滑不动
column7: 紧的：拉住绷住，没有松余|密合的：接缝合得严，不透气不漏水|拮据的：手头的钱绷得紧，动不了

column2: 中古英语 tile ← 古英语 tiġele（瓦、砖）← 原始日耳曼语 *tigulǭ ← 拉丁语 tegula（瓦）← 原始印欧语 *(s)teg-（覆盖）
column3: a thin flat piece of baked clay or stone used to cover a surface
column5: They laid white tiles in the bathroom.|A tile slipped off the roof.
column6: a thin flat slab laid alongside others to cover a surface – 一片片挨着铺开，把表面盖住的薄板
column7: 瓷砖：铺墙铺地的那种|瓦片：盖屋顶的那种

column2: 中古英语 til ← 北部古英语 til，与古诺尔斯语 til（到、直到）同出原始日耳曼语 *til（向、到）；并非 until 的缩写，反倒是 until 由它加前缀而来
column3: up to the time that
column5: We waited till the rain stopped.|The shop stays open till eleven.
column6: marking the point in time where something stops – 标出一件事到哪一刻为止
column7: 直到：持续到那一刻|在…之前：从反面说同一条界，那之前一直如此

column2: 中古英语 tilte ← 古英语 *tieltan（摇晃不稳），与形容词 tealt（不稳的）相关 ← 原始印欧语 *del-（摇、犹疑）
column3: to move into a sloping position
column5: He tilted the jug to pour.|The whole table tilts to one side.
column6: leaning off level so one end sits higher – 偏离水平，一端翘起来
column7: 倾斜：整体偏离水平|使歪：让它偏到一边去|偏向：把这份倾斜用到态度上，指偏袒一方

column2: 中古英语 tymber ← 古英语 timber ← 原始日耳曼语 *timrą（建材、房屋）← 原始印欧语 *dem-（造、建）；与德语 Zimmer（房间）同源
column3: wood prepared for building or making things
column5: The barn is built of oak timber.|They stacked the timber to dry.
column6: wood cut and kept for building with – 锯好存着、专供营造用的木头
column7: 原木：锯下来还没细加工的整段|木料：加工好、备用于制作的那些木头

column2: 中古英语 tyme ← 古英语 tīma（时候、时节）← 原始日耳曼语 *tīmô ← 原始印欧语 *deh₂y-（分开）；与 tide 同支，与拉丁语 tempus 无关
column3: what is measured in hours, days, and years
column5: We have plenty of time before the train.|I have seen it three times.
column6: the stretch in which one thing follows another – 一件接一件发生所占的那段长度
column7: 时间：可以计量的那种延续|时候：其中某一个点|次：同一事发生的第几回，把延续切成段来数

column2: 中古英语 timely ← 古英语 tīmlīċe（及时地），即 time ＋ 形容词后缀 -ly
column3: happening at just the right moment
column5: Her timely warning saved the crop.|He made a timely exit before the argument.
column6: arriving at the moment when it still helps – 赶在还来得及起作用的那一刻到
column7: 及时的：不迟，赶上了要紧的关口|适时的：时机选得正合适

column2: 源自中古法语 timide ← 拉丁语 timidus（畏怯的）← timeō（怕）
column3: lacking courage, easily frightened
column5: The timid child hid behind her mother.|He gave a timid knock at the door.
column6: holding back because fear comes first – 怕在前头，所以缩着不敢上
column7: 胆小的：遇事就怕，不敢动|羞怯的：怕的是人前露面，故显拘谨

column2: 中古英语 tin ← 古英语 tin ← 原始西日耳曼语 *tin ← 原始日耳曼语 *tiną（锡）
column3: a soft silvery metal, or a sealed metal container for food
column5: The roof is covered with sheets of tin.|Open a tin of beans for lunch.
column6: a soft light metal, and the sealed box made from it – 一种软而轻的金属，以及用它做的密封盒
column7: 锡：那种金属本身|罐头盒：用镀锡薄铁做的密封容器

column2: 中古英语 tine／tyne（极小的）＋ -y，更早词源不明
column3: extremely small
column5: A tiny crack ran across the glass.|She found a tiny shell in the sand.
column6: so small that it is easy to overlook – 小到很容易看漏
column7: 微小的：小得几乎不占分量|细小的：既小又细，多形容线状或颗状之物

column2: 中古英语 tip（末端），更早词源不明，或与 top 远亲；「小费」义另出，17 世纪始见
column3: the pointed end of something, or a small extra payment
column5: He touched the wire with the tip of a pencil.|She left a generous tip.
column6: the very end of something, or a little extra passed over – 一件东西最末那一点，或额外递过去的一点
column7: 末梢：最末那一小段|小费：额外多给的一点钱|提示：额外给出的一点信息

column2: 中古英语 tiren ← 古英语 tēorian（力竭、疲乏），更早词源不明；或出自原始西日耳曼语 *teuʀōn（停歇）
column3: to make or become weak from effort
column5: The long climb tired us all.|He never tires of telling that story.
column6: using up strength until little is left – 把力气耗到剩得不多
column7: 使疲倦：让对方力气耗掉|疲乏：自己力气耗尽的那种状态|厌倦：耗掉的不是体力而是兴致

column2: 由 tire ＋ 形容词后缀 -some 构成；tire 一支 ← 古英语 tēorian（力竭）
column3: making one feel impatient or worn out
column5: His constant questions grew tiresome.|Filling in these forms is tiresome work.
column6: going on until patience or strength runs out – 一直持续到人的耐性或力气耗光
column7: 令人厌烦的：耗掉的是耐性|累人的：耗掉的是体力

column2: 中古英语 tissu ← 古法语 tissu（织成的），是 tistre（编织）的过去分词 ← 拉丁语 texō（织）
column3: thin soft paper, or the material that living cells form in a body
column5: She dabbed her eyes with a tissue.|The scan shows damaged tissue.
column6: something woven fine and thin, whether of paper or of cells – 织得又薄又细的东西，纸的或细胞的
column7: 组织：生物体内同类细胞织成的那一层|薄纸：又软又薄、抽一张就用的那种纸

column2: 中古英语 title ← 古英语 titul ← 拉丁语 titulus（题铭、名号）
column3: the name of a book or film, or a word showing rank
column5: The title of the book is misleading.|She holds the title of chief engineer.
column6: the name put at the head to say what or who this is – 摆在最前的那个名，说明这是什么或是谁
column7: 题名：书或影片开头那个名字|头衔：人名前后表明身份的那个称号|所有权：法律上写在名下的那份权利

column2: 中古英语 tost ← 动词 tosten ← 古法语 toster（烤、炙）← 晚期拉丁语 tostare ← 拉丁语 torreō（烘、烤）；「祝酒」义 1674 年始见
column3: bread browned by heat, or words said before drinking together
column5: He had toast and jam for breakfast.|They drank a toast to the couple.
column6: bread browned by heat, and the words raised over a glass – 面包受热烤黄，以及举杯时说的那番话
column7: 吐司：切片烤过的面包|烤面包：把面包烤黄这个做法及成品|祝酒：举杯前说的那番话，旧时杯中放烤面包片增味，故得此名

column2: 1588 年始见，借自西班牙语 tabaco，或出自阿拉伯语 tubbaq，或出自加勒比土语（如 tabago，指吸烟的管子）
column3: the dried leaves used in cigarettes and pipes
column5: He rolled tobacco into a thin paper.|The shop no longer sells tobacco.
column6: dried leaves prepared to be smoked – 晾干后备着吸用的那种叶子
column7: 烟草：这种作物及其制品的通称|烟叶：具体那些晾好的叶片

column2: 中古英语 today ← 古英语 tō dæġe（在这一日），即 to ＋ day
column3: on this present day, or at the present period
column5: I have three lessons today.|Today most people carry a phone.
column6: the day one is now in – 说话时正处在的这一天
column7: 今天：眼下这一日|如今：把这一天放宽成当今这个时代

column2: 中古英语 to ← 古英语 tā ← 原始日耳曼语 *taihwǭ ← 原始印欧语 *deyḱ-（指出）
column3: one of the five parts at the end of the foot
column5: He stubbed his toe on the step.|She stood on her toes to reach it.
column6: one of the five short parts at the front of the foot – 脚前端那五个小节中的一个
column7: 脚趾：脚前端那几节的通称|足尖：整只脚最前那一处
